deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a draft for Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), Part II, around §§22-23: the zeros of θ(u−e) and the solution of the Jacobi inversion problem. The previous folio integrates Abel's differential equations. The bottom of this page is a draft of the paper's preface.

(1) Normalising the constants k_ρ. Setup: u_1,…,u_p are the normalised everywhere-finite integrals on the surface T. u_ρ has periodicity modulus πi across a_ρ and 0 across the other a-cuts. The modulus of u_ρ across b_{ρ'} is a_{ρ,ρ'}. Each u_ρ is fixed only up to an additive constant. The function θ(u_1−e_1,…,u_p−e_p) has p zeros η_1,…,η_p. With α_ρ^{(ν)} = u_ρ(η_ν), the earlier result (not on this page) reads, modulo periods:
 e_ρ ≡ Σ_{ν=1}^p α_ρ^{(ν)} + k_ρ,
where k_ρ depends only on T and on the choice of the u's.
- Riemann replaces u_ρ by u_ρ + c_ρ and e_ρ by e_ρ + c_ρ.
- Then θ(u−e), its zeros η_ν and θ itself are unchanged, while α_ρ^{(ν)} becomes α_ρ^{(ν)} + c_ρ.
- Substituting (my filled step): e_ρ + c_ρ = Σ_ν(α_ρ^{(ν)} + c_ρ) + k'_ρ, so k'_ρ = k_ρ − (p−1)c_ρ.
- Hence k_ρ vanishes for c_ρ = k_ρ/(p−1), assuming p > 1.
So one may normalise the additive constants so that e ≡ Σ α^{(ν)}. The sentence fixing this convention for the sequel is broken off.

(2) Behaviour of log θ. With k = 0, substitute v_ν = u_ν − e_ν, i.e. e_ν = Σ_μ α_ν^{(μ)}, into log θ(v_1,…,v_p). Continued continuously within T* (T cut along a, b and l), this function is larger on the positive side than on the negative side by:
- −2πi on the lines l (the image reads like '−2πi'; the transcription has '−2νi');
- 0 across a_ν;
- −2(u_ν − Σ_μ α_ν^{(μ)}) − a_{ν,ν} across b_ν.
These jumps follow from the quasi-periodicity θ(v + πi ε_ν) = θ(v) and θ(v + (a_{ν,1},…,a_{ν,p})) = e^{−2v_ν − a_{ν,ν}} θ(v).

(3) A second draft of the same statement. Put a_{ρ,ρ'} (modulus of u_ρ at b_{ρ'}) as the parameters of the θ-series of §16, and v = u − e with arbitrary constants e_1,…,e_p. One gets a single-valued function of the point of T (on T cut along a, b). It is continuous and finite off the lines a, b, and on the positive side of b_ν it is e^{2(u_ν−e_ν)+a_{ν,ν}} times its value on the negative side. This is the standard input for counting the zeros of θ(u−e) by integrating d log θ around the boundary of T'.

(4) Preface draft. Riemann writes that, as far as possible, he has avoided double notations and the introduction of his own symbols, emphasising the essential concepts instead. A crossed-out 'Gött. 1851' is followed by 'Ostern 1855 wieder aufgenommen'. He mentions the Easter and Michaelmas vacations and lectures given at Göttingen in winter 1855/56. This matches the published introduction, which refers to his lectures of 1855-56.
errors: Possible sign inconsistency between the two drafts. Passage (2) says log θ is larger on the positive side of b_ν by −2(u_ν−e_ν)−a_{ν,ν}. Passage (3) says θ there is e^{+2(u_ν−e_ν)+a_{ν,ν}} times its value on the negative side. The two agree only if u in the two passages is evaluated on different sides of b_ν or the sense of crossing is taken differently. Draft-level ambiguity, not a real error.
The normalisation c_ρ = k_ρ/(p−1) tacitly requires p ≥ 2. For p = 1 the constant k is in fact invariant under this shift. Not stated on the page.
The sentence 'Man kann daher die … additiven Constanten …' is unfinished. Several passages are fragmentary or struck through.

results.what: Under u_ρ → u_ρ + c_ρ, e_ρ → e_ρ + c_ρ, the constant k_ρ in e ≡ Σ α^{(ν)} + k becomes k_ρ − (p−1)c_ρ, so it can be normalised to 0.
results.modern_name: Riemann constant vector (its dependence on the base point / additive constants)

results.what: Jumps of log θ(u−e) across the cuts a_ν, b_ν, l of the dissected surface, from the quasi-periodicity of θ
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity of the Riemann theta function; zero count of θ(u−e) (Riemann vanishing theorem setup)

results.what: Preface draft giving the chronology: work resumed Easter 1855, lectures in winter 1855/56

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material that appears essentially verbatim in the published 1857 paper: the normalisation of the Riemann constants and the cut-jumps of log θ. The preface chronology is also already known. The crossed-out 'Gött. 1851' is a small biographical curiosity.

checkable.asserts: The choice c = k/(p−1) makes the shifted constant k − (p−1)c vanish (result 0).

checkable.sympy: n,a,v,p,c,S,k,e=symbols('n a v p c S k e'); kp = (e + c) - (S + p*c); simplify(kp - ((e - S) - (p-1)*c))
checkable.asserts: If e = S + k with S = Σ α^{(ν)}, then after α → α+c and e → e+c the new constant equals k − (p−1)c (result 0).
Term-wise check of θ(v+a) = e^{−2v−a} θ(v) for the genus-1 series θ(v) = Σ exp(a n² + 2nv), after the index shift n → n+1 (result 0).
θ(v + πi) = θ(v) term-wise for integer n (result 0).

transcription_corrections: 'auf der positiven Seite der Linie l um −2νi' — the image appears to read '−2πi' (or a multiple of πi), not '−2νi'.
The b_ν jump on the page is written '−2(u_ν − Σ_1^p α_ν^{(μ)}) − a_{ν,ν}', i.e. with e_ν already replaced by Σ α_ν^{(μ)} (consistent with k = 0).
'die Werthe der u_ρ im Punkte η_ν werden α^{(ν)}_ρ + c_ρ' — the second '+ c_ρ' in the transcription is a continuation of the inserted correction, not an extra term.
'in der Reihe des § 16' refers to the θ-series of §16 of the treatise; the crossed-out 'Gött. 1851' precedes 'Ostern 1855 wieder aufgenommen'.
